gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of calls the earbud picks last per charge. Soundcore rates the AeroClip 2 at 5 h in call mode against 8 h for music. The boom headsets last 16 h (Shokz OpenComm2 2025) and 12 h (Nuroum OpenEar Pro 2), so only they get through an 8-hour day of meetings without a recharge, and the OpenComm2 has the lowest cost per call-hour at $10.00.
standout_why: Compared against realbuyerexperiences.com (cited), openearclub.com best-for-work (cited), soundcore.com best-for-calls blog (cited as uat.soundcore.com; the uat host returned 401, so the www copy was read) and the RTINGS best-of page (it returned only navigation). RBE gives music hours only (OpenFit 2 11 h, AeroFit 2 10 h) and no prices. The Soundcore blog lists AeroClip 2 at '8H per Charge' and says its figures are music playback, not call time. Openearclub publishes the OpenComm2 UC's 16 h talk time, so that figure is partly covered, but it gives no call-time figure for any earbud. None of them states the AeroClip 2's 5 h call mode, works out the call-vs-music drop, or gives a cost per talk-hour.
decides: This confirms a boom headset as the pick for anyone on calls most of the day. On a full 8-hour meeting day the OpenComm2 (2025) finishes with about 8 h of talk time left. The AeroClip 2 runs out after 5 h and has to go back in its case. The AeroClip 2 still works for shorter call days, because its case refills about 4 call-length charges (20 h ÷ 5 h). The finding also tells the page to warn that earbud music ratings overstate call endurance: the AeroClip 2 gets 62.5% of its music time on calls.
